To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electrosensitivity of single isolated ampullae in dogfishes is about 10 times higher than previously reported.
the threshold current of the isolated ampullae of Lorenzini of the dogfish is 10 nA, and that this value depends on temperature.

the threshold currents of the isolated ampullae of Lorenzini of dogfish are 0.01–0.1 nA at temperatures of 13–19 °C, that they increase with lower (7°C) and higher temperatures by a factor of 10, that the threshold currents are about 10 times smaller than those found by other authors and that this difference might be explained by summation of the electrical input to the electrosensatory system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electrophysiological and neuroanatomical investigation of the electrosensitivities of the ampullae of Lorenzini.
the electrosensitivity of isolated ampullae of Lorenzini in the electric catfish.
the electrosensitivity of single isolated Lorenzinian organs in the dogfish (Squalus acanthias).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
electrosensitivity in the ampullary system is not only a function of temperature but also of stimulus duration and spatial summation.
the electrosensitiviy of the isolated ampullary canal is much greater than the sensitivity of the whole electrosensory apparatus of the dogfish.
the electrosensitive ampulla of the dogfish can detect electric fields as small as 2 μV/cm at 10 °C.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electrosensitivity of ampullae of Lorenzini is much higher than previously supposed.
the isolated ampulla is a good model system for studying the electrosensitivity of ampullary electroreceptors, provided that the spatial summation is taken into account.
the electrosensitive system of the dogfish is highly sensitive, and that it is capable of registering very small changes in electric field intensity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ampullae are highly sensitive to electrical stimuli.
we have developed a new method to study the electrosensitivity of single ampullae.
we have shown that the ampullae of Lorenzini are sensitive enough to respond to a wide range of electric fields.
